title: Micropulse Laser versus Eplerenone for Chronic Central Serous Chorioretinopathy: A 12-Month Comparison

license.statement: CC BY-NC 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License); private record

condition: Unilateral chronic central serous chorioretinopathy (foveal subretinal fluid for more than 6 months), no prior treatment for the disease and no macular neovascularization; retrospective two-centre comparison in which each centre used its available modality (2021-2023); 12-month follow-up

groups.description: Eyes treated at the University of Bari

groups.agent: navigated 577-nm subthreshold micropulse laser (Navilas 577s), power individualized by titration; a second session at the 90-day visit when subretinal fluid persisted
groups.description: Eyes treated at the University of Chieti-Pescara

series.notes: mean ± SD (Table 2 footnote); follow-up cells also contain p-value text after the mean ± SD; times from treatment start (baseline, 6 and 12 months); per-visit n not reported; continuous daily oral therapy over the study period

series.baseline_label: Baseline (Table 2, CMT row, NSML; row-spanned label so cells start one column earlier)
series.notes: mean ± SD (Table 2 footnote); follow-up cells also contain p-value text after the mean ± SD; times from the first laser session (baseline, 6 and 12 months); per-visit n not reported; ten eyes had the planned second session at the 90-day visit

exclusions.reason: choroidal thickness is out of scope
change values in a separate table without a stated unit; the absolute Table 2 series of the same eyes is used

exclusions.what: p-values in Table 2 cells and Table 3

notes: Visual acuity, subretinal fluid height, choroidal thickness and time to fluid resolution are also reported (not extracted).
Ambiguity resolved: the two treatments are compared without a declared experimental arm, so both groups are control.

Ambiguity resolved: continuous daily oral eplerenone does not match an injection or session schedule; regimen recorded as other. The laser arm had an initial session and retreatment only if fluid persisted; regimen recorded as prn.
